[[File:Spectral submanifold.JPG|thumb|400px|Schematic illustration of a spectral submanifold <math>\mathcal{W}(E)</math> emanating from a spectral subspace <math>E</math>. A trajectory <math>p(t)</math> in the reduced coordinates is mapped to the phase space via the manifold parametrization <math>W(p)</math>.<ref name="jain">{{Cite journal |last1=Jain |first1=Shobhit |last2=Haller |first2=George |year=2022 |title=How to compute invariant manifolds and their reduced dynamics in high-dimensional finite element models |journal=Nonlinear Dynamics |volume=107 |issue=2 |pages=1417–1450 |doi=10.1007/s11071-021-06957-4 |s2cid=232269982|doi-access=free |hdl=20.500.11850/519249 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>]]
In [[dynamical system]]s, a '''spectral submanifold''' (SSM) is the unique [[Differentiable manifold#Definition|smoothest]] [[invariant manifold]] serving as the nonlinear extension of a spectral subspace of a [[linear dynamical system]] under the addition of nonlinearities.<ref name="nnm">{{Cite journal |last1=Haller |first1=George |last2=Ponsioen |first2=Sten |date=2016 |title=Nonlinear normal modes and spectral submanifolds: Existence, uniqueness and use in model reduction |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11071-016-2974-z |journal=Nonlinear Dynamics |volume=86 |issue=3 |pages=1493–1534 |arxiv=1602.00560 |doi=10.1007/s11071-016-2974-z |s2cid=44074026}}</ref> SSM theory provides conditions for when invariant properties of eigenspaces of a linear dynamical system can be extended to a [[nonlinear system]], and therefore motivates the use of SSMs in [[nonlinear dimensionality reduction]].

SSMs are chiefly employed for the exact model reduction of dynamical systems. For the automated computation of SSMs and the analysis of the reduced dynamics, open source online software packages such as '''SSMTool''' and '''SSMLearn''' have been published. These tools allow to study system dynamics either from the underlying equations of motion or from trajectory data, supporting both analytical and data-driven approaches.<ref>{{Citation |last=Jain |first=Shobhit |title=SSMTool 2.6: Computation of invariant manifolds in high-dimensional mechanics problems |date=2024-10-09 |url=https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13909795 |access-date=2024-11-12 |publisher=[object Object] |doi=10.5281/zenodo.13909795 |last2=Li |first2=Mingwu |last3=Thurnher |first3=Thomas |last4=Haller |first4=George}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=haller-group/SSMLearn |date=2024-11-12 |url=https://github.com/haller-group/SSMLearn |access-date=2024-11-12 |publisher=Haller Group, Nonlinear Dynamics}}</ref> Detailed documentation for SSMTool is provided online.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SSMTool |url=https://ssmtool.mae.sustech.edu.cn/ |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=ssmtool.mae.sustech.edu.cn}}</ref>

==Definition==
Consider a nonlinear [[ordinary differential equation]] of the form
:<math>\frac{dx}{dt} = Ax + f_0(x),\quad x\in \R^n,</math>
with constant matrix <math>\ A\in \R^{n\times n}</math> and the nonlinearities contained in the smooth function <math>f_0 = \mathcal{O}(|x|^2)</math>.

Assume that <math>\text{Re} \lambda_j < 0</math> for all eigenvalues <math>\lambda_j,\ j = 1,\ldots, n</math> of <math>A</math>, that is, the origin is an asymptotically stable fixed point. Now select a span <math>E = \text{span}\, \{v^E_{1},\ldots v^E_{m}\}</math> of <math>m</math> [[eigenvector]]s <math>v^E_{i}</math> of <math>A</math>. Then, the eigenspace <math>E</math> is an [[invariant subspace]] of the linearized system
:<math>\frac{dx}{dt} = Ax,\quad x\in \R^n.</math>

Under addition of the nonlinearity <math>f_0</math> to the linear system, <math>E</math> generally perturbs into infinitely many invariant manifolds. Among these invariant manifolds, the unique smoothest one is referred to as the spectral submanifold.

An equivalent result for unstable SSMs holds for <math>\text{Re} \lambda_j > 0</math>. 

===Existence===
The spectral submanifold tangent to <math>E</math> at the origin is guaranteed to exist provided that certain non-resonance conditions are satisfied by the eigenvalues <math>\lambda^E_i</math> in the spectrum of <math>E</math>.<ref name="cabre">{{Cite journal |last1=Cabré |first1=P. |last2=Fontich |first2=E. |last3=de la Llave |first3=R. |date=2003 |title=The parametrization method for invariant manifolds I: manifolds associated to non-resonant spectral subspaces |journal=Indiana Univ. Math. J. |volume=52 |pages=283–328 |doi=10.1512/iumj.2003.52.2245 |hdl=2117/876|hdl-access=free }}</ref> In particular, there can be no linear combination of <math>\lambda^E_i</math> equal to one of the eigenvalues of <math>A</math> outside of the spectral subspace. If there is such an outer resonance, one can include the resonant mode into <math>E</math> and extend the analysis to a higher-dimensional SSM pertaining to the extended spectral subspace.

==Non-autonomous extension==
The theory on spectral submanifolds extends to nonlinear [[Non-autonomous system (mathematics)|non-autonomous system]]s of the form
:<math>\frac{dx}{dt} = Ax + f_0(x) + \epsilon f_1(x, \Omega t),\quad \Omega\in \mathbb{T}^k,\ 0\le \epsilon \ll 1,</math>
with <math>f_1 : \R^n \times \mathbb{T}^k \to \R^n</math> a [[Quasiperiodic motion|quasiperiodic]] forcing term.<ref name="haro">{{Cite journal |last1=Haro |first1=A. |last2=de la Llave |first2=R. |date=2006 |title=A parameterisation method for the computation of invariant tori and their whiskers in quasiperiodic maps: Rigorous results |journal=Differ. Equ. |volume=228 |issue=2 |pages=530–579 |bibcode=2006JDE...228..530H |doi=10.1016/j.jde.2005.10.005|doi-access= }}</ref>

==Significance==
Spectral submanifolds are useful for rigorous nonlinear dimensionality reduction in dynamical systems. The reduction of a high-dimensional phase space to a lower-dimensional manifold can lead to major simplifications by allowing for an accurate description of the system's main asymptotic behaviour.<ref name="rega">{{Cite journal |last1=Rega |first1=Giuseppe |last2=Troger |first2=Hans |date=2005 |title=Dimension Reduction of Dynamical Systems: Methods, Models, Applications |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226099099 |journal=Nonlinear Dynamics |volume=41 |issue=1–3 |pages=1–15 |doi=10.1007/s11071-005-2790-3 |s2cid=14728580}}</ref> For a known dynamical system, SSMs can be computed analytically by solving the invariance equations, and reduced models on SSMs may be employed for prediction of the response to forcing.<ref name="ponsioen18">{{Cite journal |last1=Ponsioen |first1=Sten |last2=Pedergnana |first2=Tiemo |last3=Haller |first3=George |date=2018 |title=Automated computation of autonomous spectral submanifolds for nonlinear modal analysis |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022460X18300701 |journal=Journal of Sound and Vibration |volume=420 |pages=269–295 |arxiv=1709.00886 |bibcode=2018JSV...420..269P |doi=10.1016/j.jsv.2018.01.048 |s2cid=44186335}}</ref>

Furthermore these manifolds may also be extracted directly from trajectory data of a dynamical system with the use of machine learning algorithms.<ref name="datassm">{{Cite journal |last1=Cenedese |first1=Mattia |last2=Axås |first2=Joar |last3=Bäuerlein |first3=Bastian |last4=Avila |first4=Kerstin |last5=Haller |first5=George |date=2022 |title=Data-driven modeling and prediction of non-linearizable dynamics via spectral submanifolds |journal=Nature Communications |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=872 |doi=10.1038/s41467-022-28518-y  |doi-access=free|pmc=8847615 |pmid=35169152|arxiv=2201.04976 |bibcode=2022NatCo..13..872C }}</ref>
